example_sentence.english: Please set the table for four guests.
example_sentence.croatian: Molim vas, postavite stol za četiri gosta.
example_sentence.german: Bitte decken Sie den Tisch für vier Gäste.

quiz.question: What is the German word for 'table'?
quiz.explanation: 'der Tisch' is the German masculine noun for table. 'der Stuhl' means chair, 'das Bett' means bed, 'die Lampe' means lamp.

example_sentence.english: We need an extra chair for this table.
example_sentence.croatian: Trebamo dodatnu stolicu za ovaj stol.
example_sentence.german: Wir brauchen einen zusätzlichen Stuhl für diesen Tisch.

quiz.question: How do you say 'chair' in Croatian?
quiz.explanation: 'stolica' is the Croatian word for chair. 'stol' means table, 'krevet' means bed, 'ormar' means wardrobe.

example_sentence.english: Here is your menu, sir. I'll be back to take your order.
example_sentence.croatian: Evo vašeg jelovnika, gospodine. Vratit ću se uzeti vašu narudžbu.
example_sentence.german: Hier ist Ihre Speisekarte, mein Herr. Ich komme zurück, um Ihre Bestellung aufzunehmen.

quiz.question: What is the Croatian word for 'menu'?
quiz.explanation: 'jelovnik' is the Croatian word for menu. 'račun' means bill, 'kuhinja' means kitchen, 'piće' means drink.

example_sentence.english: Please bring a clean plate for the guest.
example_sentence.croatian: Molim vas, donesite čisti tanjur za gosta.
example_sentence.german: Bitte bringen Sie einen sauberen Teller für den Gast.

quiz.question: What is the English word for 'der Teller'?
quiz.explanation: 'der Teller' translates to 'plate' in English. 'cup' is Tasse, 'bowl' is Schüssel, 'spoon' is Löffel.

example_sentence.english: Set the knife on the right side of the plate.
example_sentence.croatian: Stavite nož s desne strane tanjura.
example_sentence.german: Legen Sie das Messer auf die rechte Seite des Tellers.

quiz.question: How do you say 'knife' in German?
quiz.explanation: 'das Messer' is the German neuter noun for knife. 'die Gabel' is fork, 'der Löffel' is spoon, 'die Tasse' is cup.

example_sentence.english: The fork goes on the left side of the plate.
example_sentence.croatian: Vilica ide s lijeve strane tanjura.
example_sentence.german: Die Gabel kommt auf die linke Seite des Tellers.

quiz.question: What is the Croatian word for 'fork'?
quiz.explanation: 'vilica' means fork in Croatian. 'nož' means knife, 'žlica' means spoon, 'tanjur' means plate.

example_sentence.english: Please bring a soup spoon for the guest.
example_sentence.croatian: Molim vas, donesite žlicu za juhu za gosta.
example_sentence.german: Bitte bringen Sie einen Suppenlöffel für den Gast.

quiz.question: Which is the correct German article for 'Löffel'?
quiz.explanation: 'Löffel' is a masculine noun in German, so it takes 'der' as its definite article.

example_sentence.english: Fold the napkin neatly beside the plate.
example_sentence.german: Falten Sie die Serviette ordentlich neben den Teller.

quiz.question: What is the German word for 'napkin'?
quiz.explanation: 'die Serviette' is the German word for napkin. 'das Tuch' is cloth, 'der Lappen' is rag, 'die Decke' is blanket.

example_sentence.english: This tablecloth is stained. Please change it immediately.
example_sentence.croatian: Ovaj stolnjak je zamrljan. Molim vas, odmah ga promijenite.
example_sentence.german: Diese Tischdecke ist fleckig. Bitte wechseln Sie sie sofort.

quiz.question: How do you say 'tablecloth' in Croatian?
quiz.explanation: 'stolnjak' is the Croatian word for tablecloth. 'ručnik' is towel, 'plahta' is sheet, 'zavjesa' is curtain.

example_sentence.english: Please leave your key at the front desk when you check out.
example_sentence.croatian: Molim vas, ostavite ključ na recepciji prilikom odjave.
example_sentence.german: Bitte lassen Sie Ihren Schlüssel bei der Abreise an der Rezeption.

quiz.question: What is the German word for 'front desk' in a hotel?
quiz.explanation: 'die Rezeption' is the German word for hotel front desk. 'der Eingang' is entrance, 'das Zimmer' is room, 'die Halle' is hall.

example_sentence.english: The bellhop will bring a luggage cart for your suitcases.
example_sentence.croatian: Nosač će donijeti kolica za vašu prtljagu.
example_sentence.german: Der Hotelpage bringt einen Gepäckwagen für Ihre Koffer.

quiz.question: How do you say 'luggage cart' in Croatian?
quiz.explanation: 'kolica za prtljagu' means luggage cart. 'vreća za smeće' is trash bag, 'nosiljka' is stretcher, 'invalidska kolica' is wheelchair.

example_sentence.english: Shake the ingredients vigorously in the cocktail shaker.
example_sentence.croatian: Snažno protresite sastojke u shakeru za koktele.
example_sentence.german: Schütteln Sie die Zutaten kräftig im Cocktailshaker.

quiz.question: What is the German term for 'cocktail shaker'?
quiz.explanation: 'der Cocktailshaker' is the German term. 'der Mixer' is blender, 'das Glas' is glass, 'der Löffel' is spoon.

example_sentence.english: Please bring two wine glasses for the red wine.
example_sentence.croatian: Molim vas, donesite dvije vinske čaše za crno vino.
example_sentence.german: Bitte bringen Sie zwei Weingläser für den Rotwein.

quiz.question: How do you say 'wine glass' in Croatian?
quiz.explanation: 'vinska čaša' is wine glass. 'pivska čaša' is beer glass, 'čaša za vodu' is water glass, 'šalica' is cup.

example_sentence.english: Please vacuum the carpet in room 204.
example_sentence.croatian: Molim vas, usisajte tepih u sobi 204.
example_sentence.german: Bitte saugen Sie den Teppich in Zimmer 204.

quiz.question: What is the German word for 'vacuum cleaner'?
quiz.explanation: 'der Staubsauger' is vacuum cleaner. 'der Besen' is broom, 'der Mopp' is mop, 'der Eimer' is bucket.

example_sentence.english: Restock the cleaning trolley with fresh towels before starting.
example_sentence.croatian: Napunite kolica za čišćenje svježim ručnicima prije početka.
example_sentence.german: Füllen Sie den Reinigungswagen mit frischen Handtüchern auf, bevor Sie anfangen.

quiz.question: How do you say 'cleaning trolley' in Croatian?
quiz.explanation: 'kolica za čišćenje' is cleaning trolley. 'kolica za prtljagu' is luggage cart, 'kolica za hranu' is food cart, 'dječja kolica' is stroller.

example_sentence.english: Would you like a cup of coffee with your breakfast?
example_sentence.croatian: Želite li šalicu kave uz doručak?
example_sentence.german: Möchten Sie eine Tasse Kaffee zu Ihrem Frühstück?

quiz.question: What is the Croatian word for 'coffee'?
quiz.explanation: 'kava' is coffee. 'čaj' is tea, 'mlijeko' is milk, 'sok' is juice.

example_sentence.english: Fresh bread is served with every meal.
example_sentence.croatian: Svježi kruh se poslužuje uz svaki obrok.
example_sentence.german: Frisches Brot wird zu jeder Mahlzeit serviert.

quiz.question: Which German article goes with 'Brot'?
quiz.explanation: 'Brot' is a neuter noun, so it takes 'das'.

conversation_scenarios.situation: Welcoming a guest at a restaurant

customer_message.croatian: Dobar dan, stol za dvoje molim.
customer_message.german: Hallo, einen Tisch für zwei bitte.

correct_response.english: Good evening! Right this way, please. Do you prefer inside or on the terrace?
correct_response.croatian: Dobra večer! Ovuda molim. Želite li unutra ili na terasi?
correct_response.german: Guten Abend! Hier entlang bitte. Möchten Sie drinnen oder auf der Terrasse sitzen?

conversation_scenarios.tips: Always greet with a smile and offer choice. In Croatia, 'Dobra večer' is used after sunset. In Germany, use formal 'Sie' for guests.

conversation_scenarios.situation: Taking a drink order at a bar

customer_message.english: I'd like a cold beer please. What do you have on tap?
customer_message.croatian: Htio bih hladno pivo. Što imate točeno?
customer_message.german: Ich hätte gern ein kaltes Bier. Was haben Sie vom Fass?

correct_response.english: We have local Croatian lager, German pilsner, and wheat beer on tap.
correct_response.croatian: Imamo domaći hrvatski lager, njemački pilsner i pšenično pivo točeno.
correct_response.german: Wir haben kroatisches Lager, deutsches Pilsner und Weizenbier vom Fass.

conversation_scenarios.tips: Know your beer types. 'Točeno' in Croatian means on tap. German 'vom Fass' literally means 'from the barrel'.

customer_message.english: Good evening, I have a reservation under the name Müller.
customer_message.croatian: Dobra večer, imam rezervaciju pod imenom Müller.
customer_message.german: Guten Abend, ich habe eine Reservierung auf den Namen Müller.

correct_response.english: Welcome, Mr. Müller. I've found your booking. You've reserved a deluxe room for three nights. May I see your passport please?
correct_response.croatian: Dobrodošli, gospodine Müller. Našao sam vašu rezervaciju. Rezervirali ste deluxe sobu na tri noći. Mogu li vidjeti vašu putovnicu?
correct_response.german: Willkommen, Herr Müller. Ich habe Ihre Buchung gefunden. Sie haben ein Deluxe-Zimmer für drei Nächte reserviert. Darf ich bitte Ihren Reisepass sehen?

wrong_options.english: Sorry, no reservation under that name.
wrong_options.croatian: Oprostite, nema rezervacije pod tim imenom.
wrong_options.german: Entschuldigung, keine Reservierung unter diesem Namen.

conversation_scenarios.tips: Always confirm the reservation details. In Germany and Croatia, guests must present ID upon check-in by law.

customer_message.english: Excuse me, this soup is completely cold. I can't eat this.
customer_message.croatian: Oprostite, ova juha je potpuno hladna. Ne mogu ovo jesti.
customer_message.german: Entschuldigung, diese Suppe ist völlig kalt. Ich kann das nicht essen.

correct_response.english: I sincerely apologize for this. Let me take it back immediately and bring you a fresh, hot bowl. It will be just a few minutes.
correct_response.croatian: Iskreno se ispričavam zbog ovoga. Odmah ću to odnijeti i donijeti vam svježu, vruću zdjelu. Bit će gotovo za nekoliko minuta.
correct_response.german: Ich entschuldige mich aufrichtig dafür. Ich nehme es sofort zurück und bringe Ihnen eine frische, heiße Schüssel. Es dauert nur ein paar Minuten.

wrong_options.english: It's supposed to be cold soup.
wrong_options.croatian: To bi trebala biti hladna juha.
wrong_options.german: Es soll eine kalte Suppe sein.

wrong_options.english: I can microwave it for you.
wrong_options.croatian: Mogu vam to podgrijati u mikrovalnoj.
wrong_options.german: Ich kann es für Sie in der Mikrowelle aufwärmen.

conversation_scenarios.tips: Never argue with the guest. Apologize sincerely and offer an immediate solution. Do not offer to microwave food in fine dining settings.

english_phonetics.description: English pronunciation guide for hospitality terms

th_voiced.tip: Vocal cords vibrate, tongue between teeth

schwa.tip: Most common sound, relaxed neutral vowel

croatian_phonetics.description: Croatian pronunciation guide for hospitality terms

ć.tip: Softer than č, tongue touches palate

r.tip: Rolled r, tip of tongue vibrates

german_phonetics.description: German pronunciation guide for hospitality terms

ch_soft.tip: After i, e, ä, ö, ü - hissing sound

ch_hard.tip: After a, o, u - like Scottish 'loch'

polite_expressions.title: Formal Address in German
polite_expressions.rule: Always use 'Sie' (formal you) with guests, never 'du' (informal you).
polite_expressions.example_correct: Möchten Sie etwas trinken? (Would you like something to drink?)
polite_expressions.example_wrong: Willst du etwas trinken? (Too informal - do not use)
polite_expressions.context: Used in all German-speaking hospitality settings

polite_expressions.title: Croatian Formal Address
polite_expressions.rule: Use 'Vi' (capitalized, formal you) and 2nd person plural verb forms with guests.
polite_expressions.example_correct: Kako ste danas, gospodine? (How are you today, sir?)
polite_expressions.example_wrong: Kako si danas? (Informal - only for friends)
polite_expressions.context: Standard in all Croatian service environments

polite_expressions.title: Polite Requests in English
polite_expressions.rule: Use 'would', 'could', or 'may' for polite requests rather than 'can' or 'want'.
polite_expressions.example_correct: Would you like to see the wine list?
polite_expressions.example_wrong: Do you want the wine list?

polite_expressions.title: German Subjunctive for Politeness
polite_expressions.rule: Use Konjunktiv II (subjunctive) forms like 'hätten', 'wären', 'möchten' for very polite requests.
polite_expressions.example_correct: Ich hätte gern einen Kaffee. (I would like a coffee.)
polite_expressions.example_wrong: Ich will einen Kaffee. (I want a coffee - too direct.)

polite_expressions.title: Croatian Conditional for Offers
polite_expressions.rule: Use 'biste li' or 'želite li' for polite offers and suggestions.
polite_expressions.example_correct: Želite li još jedno piće? (Would you like another drink?)
polite_expressions.example_wrong: Hoćeš još jedno piće? (Do you want another - too rough.)

common_mistakes.correction: When bringing something to a guest, 'mitbringen' is more natural.
common_mistakes.example_correct: Ich bringe Ihnen die Speisekarte mit.

Check IN at a hotel, check OUT of a hotel.
common_mistakes.example_wrong: I will check out the hotel at 3 PM.
common_mistakes.example_correct: I will check into the hotel at 3 PM.
